A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LATR research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results on logical and mathematical reasoning, alongside component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds experiments with additional base models, an EPTree comparator, and further ablations and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 retain the same branching, lookahead simulation, edit-distance pruning, stochastic fallback, and annealed hybrid rollout procedure. Newly tested pruning and lookahead variants are experimental ablations; the proposed LATR method is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Countdown, DAPO Math, MATH-500, AMC-2023, and Olympiad-Bench for the same reasoning tasks. Additional base-model experiments use the existing Countdown setting and do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds TreeRL's EPTree rollout strategy under both GRPO and DAPO in Table 7. v1's selection-based rollout strategy, SR, becomes RDS with the same described 16-to-8 BLEU/ROUGE-based selection procedure. The component comparisons also gain token-level-lookahead and embedding-based-pruning variants.

E3.justification: Evaluation configurations expand to Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-1.7B-Base, with additional EPTree generation/subsampling and branching/pruning threshold-sweep protocols. Original splits, the 500-step training budget, and eight-completion evaluation remain unchanged. The stated temperature grid drops 2.0, matching its absence from the unchanged original plot; this does not establish rerunning that experiment.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct token-level versus trajectory-level lookahead ablation, embedding-based similarity analysis, and separate sensitivity sweeps for both branching thresholds and the pruning threshold. These substantially extend evidence about LATR's design choices. Rollout-count scalability is retained and moved from Appendix C.1 to Section 5.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Eight sampled evaluation completions and descriptive sensitivity comparisons are retained without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for additional base models, EPTree, token-level lookahead, embedding pruning, and threshold sweeps. For example, its new Qwen2.5-7B comparison reports Pass@1 of 76.0 for LATR versus 70.9 for stochastic sampling. Original Tables 1–4 and plotted results are retained. DAPO+SR/RDS average Pass@1 completion length changes from 248 to 348 in v1 Table 6 versus v3 Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of LATR, GRPO/DAPO objectives, reward definitions, and O(nk) bound are retained. Equation 10 renames the training-step index without changing the annealing rule. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: trajectory-level diversity through lookahead tree rollouts compatible with existing policy updates. The headline claims of 131% faster learning and 4.2% higher Pass@1 remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for weaknesses of token-level lookahead and embedding similarity, and attributes TreeRL's gains primarily to policy updates following the EPTree comparison. Runtime overhead is reattributed from GPU memory/cache behavior to sequential per-sequence operations. The new pruning-threshold explanation in Appendix C.3 reverses the direction implied by Equation 7.

D1.justification: v3 specifies EPTree parameters, random subsampling, integration of TreeRL's official code into VeRL, and the Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B similarity model. Core implementation settings, hardware, data-transformation prompt, and code/data access information remain unchanged. EPTree documentation is internally inconsistent: its formula and (4,2,1) parameters imply 12 sequences, while the text states 10.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially expands positioning against lookahead reasoning through Tree-of-Thoughts, MCTS-DPO, ReST-MCTS, and Quiet-STaR, distinguishing diversity promotion from reward propagation and step-level supervision. TreeRL/TreePO discussion is reorganized, and RDS gains attribution to Xu et al. References to Stepwise Informativeness Search and the 2017 AlphaGo work are removed.

P1.justification: Reorganization is concentrated in the discussions, related work, and Appendix C: rollout-count analysis moves into the main text, while alternative-rollout comparisons move to the appendix. Related work is rewritten, terminology is refined, acknowledgments are added, and the publication header changes. Most introductory, methodological, and main-results prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Existing figure artwork is retained, with rollout-count and temperature plots combined into v3 Figure 4. New base-model and threshold tables are added, and ablation, comparator, and similarity tables gain rows. Other displays are relocated, resized, or renumbered within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through additional base models, a direct lookahead ablation, threshold and similarity analyses, and a tree-rollout comparator. Expanded related work also clarifies the contribution. These benefits support a limited overall improvement, tempered by the inconsistent EPTree sequence count in Appendix C.1 and the reversed threshold explanation in Appendix C.3, which weaken parts of the new evidence's reproducibility and interpretation.
